subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core `bootstrap-extra-files` hook contract?
rationale: This controls which workspace files enter deterministic system-prompt context and changes a config-driven file-loading boundary, so automation should not decide the product/security contract alone.

options.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the hook path after the linked PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, session filtering, and upgrade-safe docs.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and keep users on first-class workspace filenames or manual context-loading patterns.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Keep this issue open as design input for a broader context API rather than landing the current hook-specific shape.

recommendation.title: Approve Repaired Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the hook path after the linked PR or replacement preserves guards, budgets, session filtering, and upgrade-safe docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook PR and has recent direct history on the workspace bootstrap loader boundary.
